info.text:
You don't need a perfect 850 to get the best rates.
Only 1.71% of consumers had an 850 FICO Score in June 2026 (Experian).
Fannie Mae's top mortgage pricing tier starts at 780 (LLPA Matrix updated Sept. 30, 2026).
Our math: on a $400,000 purchase loan with 20% down, a 780 and an 850 get the same 0.375% loan-level price adjustment, $1,500. Difference: $0. Lenders often build it into your rate instead of charging it at closing, and other adjustments can apply.
Experian's top auto tier, super prime (781-850 on VantageScore 4.0), averaged a 4.41% new-car APR in Q2 2026.
Sources: Fannie Mae LLPA Matrix; Experian.
News and education, not financial advice.
